topic: Area of study 1: Western classical tradition 1650-1910
outcome: Listen to unfamiliar music from the Baroque concerto, Mozart opera and Romantic piano strands and describe its elements in musical language.

topic: Area of study 1: Western classical tradition 1650-1910
outcome: Analyse set work excerpts: effect of audience, time and place, how strands differ, composer purpose and links between elements and context.

topic: Area of study 1: Western classical tradition 1650-1910
outcome: Know the set concertos by Purcell, Vivaldi and Bach and their Baroque features.

topic: Area of study 1: Western classical tradition 1650-1910
outcome: Know the Act 1 numbers from Le Nozze di Figaro: overture, duettini, cavatina, arias and terzetto.

topic: Area of study 1: Western classical tradition 1650-1910
subtopic: Piano music of Chopin, Brahms and Grieg
outcome: Know the set piano works by Chopin, Brahms and Grieg.

topic: Area of study 1: Western classical tradition 1650-1910
outcome: Describe melodic contour, intervals, ornaments, passing and auxiliary notes, and devices; identify diatonic and chromatic harmony, cadences, pedals and suspensions.

topic: Area of study 1: Western classical tradition 1650-1910
outcome: Identify modulations, enharmonic keys, binary, ternary, ritornello, sonata form, recitative and aria structures.

topic: Area of study 1: Western classical tradition 1650-1910
outcome: Describe orchestral and vocal timbres, string and piano techniques, textures from monophonic to fugal, tempo terms, syncopation, hemiola, and dynamics and articulation.

topic: Area of study 1: Western classical tradition 1650-1910
outcome: Read four to eight bar excerpts of unfamiliar music and about two pages of familiar scores; write melodic and rhythmic notation in all keys.

topic: Area of study 1: Western classical tradition 1650-1910
outcome: Identify standard and extended chords, inversions and secondary dominant sevenths, aurally and in notation, using correct terminology.

topic: Areas of study 2-7: general requirements
outcome: Choose two areas from pop, music for media, theatre, jazz, contemporary traditional and art music since 1910.

topic: Areas of study 2-7: general requirements
outcome: Listen to unfamiliar music by all named artists and appraise three artists per area using at least two published works and changes in style over time.

topic: Areas of study 2-7: general requirements
outcome: Read passages of up to eight bars, identify chords and symbols, and use terminology for the chosen areas.

topic: Area of study 2: Pop music
outcome: Know the style of pop music and the named artists: Stevie Wonder, Joni Mitchell, Muse, Beyonce, Daft Punk, Labrinth.

topic: Area of study 2: Pop music
outcome: Describe riffs, hooks, melisma, bends and slides, blue notes; power chords, sus4, extended chords and chord symbols.

topic: Area of study 2: Pop music
outcome: Identify modes, pentatonic and blues scales; intro, verse, chorus, middle 8, bridge and breakdown.

topic: Area of study 2: Pop music
outcome: Describe studio effects, instrument and vocal timbres, looping and layering, bpm, groove, backbeat and fades.

topic: Area of study 3: Music for media
outcome: Know the style of music for media and the named artists: Bernard Herrmann, Hans Zimmer, Michael Giacchino, Thomas Newman, Nobuo Uematsu.

topic: Area of study 3: Music for media
outcome: Describe leitmotif, extended and complex chords, tonal, atonal and modal writing.

topic: Area of study 3: Music for media
outcome: Explain cue, underscore, mickey-mousing, diegetic and non-diegetic music; orchestral, electronic and ethnic timbres and effects.

topic: Area of study 3: Music for media
outcome: Identify clusters, polarised texture, drones, additive rhythm, cross rhythm and rhythmic layering.

topic: Area of study 4: Music for theatre
outcome: Know the style of music for theatre and the named artists: Kurt Weill, Richard Rodgers, Stephen Sondheim, Claude-Michel Schonberg, Jason Robert Brown.

topic: Area of study 4: Music for theatre
outcome: Describe pitch bends, melisma, leitmotif, angular melody; power, sus4 and extended chords.

topic: Area of study 4: Music for theatre
outcome: Identify song structures and orchestral, contemporary and vocal timbres and techniques.

topic: Area of study 4: Music for theatre
outcome: Identify a cappella and colla voce textures, bpm and irregular metre.

topic: Area of study 5: Jazz
outcome: Know the style of jazz and the named artists: Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington, Charlie Parker, Miles Davis, Pat Metheny, Gwilym Simcock.

topic: Area of study 5: Jazz
outcome: Describe smears, falls, rips, glissandi; extended chords, tritone substitution and turn-arounds.

topic: Area of study 5: Jazz
outcome: Identify blue notes, blues, pentatonic, octatonic scales, modal jazz, 12-bar blues, head, chorus and fours.

topic: Area of study 5: Jazz
outcome: Describe mutes, growl, ghosted notes, big band instruments, heterophony, swing, push and drag, stop time.

topic: Area of study 6: Contemporary traditional music
outcome: Know the style of contemporary traditional music and the named artists: Astor Piazzolla, Toumani Diabate, Anoushka Shankar, Mariza, Bellowhead.

topic: Area of study 6: Contemporary traditional music
outcome: Describe raga, kumbengo, birimintingo, drones, sus4 chords and modes.

topic: Area of study 6: Contemporary traditional music
outcome: Identify tango nuevo, milonga, fado, alap, fusion, folk rock; bandoneon, kora, sitar, Portuguese guitar and tango string techniques.

topic: Area of study 6: Contemporary traditional music
outcome: Identify looping, layering, heterophony, polyrhythm, 3+3+2, habanera and tala.

topic: Area of study 7: Art music since 1910
outcome: Know the style of art music since 1910 and the named artists: Dmitri Shostakovich, Olivier Messiaen, Steve Reich, James MacMillan.

topic: Area of study 7: Art music since 1910
subtopic: Art music melody, harmony and tonality
outcome: Describe modes of limited transposition, tone rows, resultant melody, metamorphosis, non-functional and static harmony, clusters, bitonality and atonality.

topic: Area of study 7: Art music since 1910
outcome: Identify cyclical structures, ostinato, cadenza; organ stops, ondes Martenot, studio effects and extended techniques.

topic: Area of study 7: Art music since 1910
outcome: Identify looping, layering, drones, additive and palindromic rhythms, metrical displacement, phasing, augmentation and diminution.

topic: Performance
outcome: Perform at least ten minutes as an instrumentalist or vocalist, solo or in ensemble, and/or through music production.

topic: Performance
outcome: Choose repertoire by the demand of your own part and play pieces with composer-intended accompaniment accompanied.

topic: Performance
outcome: Show control of pitch, rhythm, tone and ensemble, and tempo, dynamics, phrasing and articulation, with understanding of style and the composer's purpose.

topic: Performance
outcome: Realise a pre-existing piece with MIDI and audio tracks, at least five student-input tracks, with good capture and dynamic processing.

topic: Performance
outcome: Supply a score, lead sheet, guide recording or annotation with each performance recording.

topic: Composition
outcome: Develop and manipulate musical ideas into two musically convincing compositions: one to an externally set brief, one free.

topic: Composition
outcome: Compose at least four and a half minutes in total, as notated or lead sheet work, or digital production with annotation.

topic: Composition
outcome: Use musical elements with technical control and creativity in your chosen style or genre.

topic: Composition
outcome: Write a 150-word programme note for each piece on intention and audience, list software and hardware, and supply score, lead sheet or aural guide.
